Chevalley basis

Words: 201 Articles: 3
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A Chevalley basis of a complex semisimple Lie algebra consists of suitable coroot elements and one vector eα​ in each root space, chosen so all Lie bracket structure constants are integers. In particular [eα​,eβ​]=Nα,β​eα+β​ when the sum is a root, with Nα,β​=±(p+1) where β−pα is the last negative-direction root in the root string. For independent roots with no root sum the bracket is zero. The integral lattice makes reduction to other fields possible.

Serre relations ((adei​)1−aij​ej​=0)

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Chevalley basis OurBigBook.com
For simple-root generators ei​,fi​,hi​ with [hi​,ej​]=aij​ej​, the Serre relations include [ei​,fj​]=δij​hi​ and (adei​)1−aij​ej​=(adfi​)1−aij​fj​=0 for i=j. The off-diagonal Cartan entries are nonpositive integers. These relations restrict which iterated simple-root brackets remain nonzero.

SU(2) proof of the Serre relations

Words: 48
Serre relations OurBigBook.com
For distinct simple roots, αj​−αi​ has mixed-sign simple-root coefficients and is not a root. Thus [fi​,ej​]=0. In the finite-dimensional adjoint representation of the simple-root SU(2) subalgebra, ej​ is a lowest-weight vector of weight aij​. Standard SU(2) ladders force aij​=−nij​ with nij​≥0 integral and make (adei​)nij​+1ej​=0.

Simply laced Chevalley commutator formula (xs​(u)−1xr​(t)−1xs​(u)xr​(t)=xr+s​(−Nr,s​tu))

Words: 55
Chevalley basis OurBigBook.com
For equal-length roots r,s with a root sum, their angle is 2π/3. The vectors 2r+s and r+2s have squared length three times a root's squared length, so neither is a root. Thus [er​,er+s​]=[es​,er+s​]=0. Apply the central-commutator exponential identity to A=tader​ and B=uades​, whose commutator is tuNr,s​ader+s​, to obtain the displayed identity over the complex numbers.

Jordan decomposition in an abstract semisimple Lie algebra (x=xs​+xn​)

Words: 83
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A complex semisimple Lie algebra has an intrinsic Jordan–Chevalley decomposition x=xs​+xn​ characterized by [xs​,xn​]=0, a diagonalizable Adjoint representation operator adxs​, and a nilpotent Adjoint representation operator adxn​. The Adjoint representation is faithful because the centre is zero. Closure of semisimple matrix Lie algebras are closed under additive Jordan decomposition applied to this faithful representation supplies the parts and their uniqueness. For every finite-dimensional Lie algebra representation ρ, the operators ρ(xs​) and ρ(xn​) are the semisimple and nilpotent parts of ρ(x). Thus the decomposition is independent of a matrix embedding; for a nonfaithful representation it passes to the semisimple quotient by its kernel.

Split semisimple Lie algebra (g=h⊕⨁α​gα​over the ground field)

Words: 64
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A semisimple Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero is split if it has a Cartan subalgebra whose adjoint action is simultaneously diagonalizable over that field. Its root-space decomposition then needs no extension of scalars. The sl2R Lie algebra is split, with the real diagonal Cartan subalgebra. The real special unitary Lie algebra su(2) is not: its adjoint operators are skew-adjoint for the positive definite inner product obtained by negating its Killing form. Thus a split adjoint operator would have to be zero.

Compact real form of a complex semisimple Lie algebra (u⊗R​C≅g)

Words: 61
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A compact real form of a complex semisimple Lie algebra g is a real Lie subalgebra u whose complexification of a Lie algebra is g and whose Killing form is negative definite. Its simply connected Lie group is compact. The positive internal inner product used in unitary gauge theory is therefore −κ. For sl2​(C) the SU(2) Lie algebra is a compact real form, whereas sl2​(R) is a different real form with indefinite Killing form.

Perfect Lie algebra

Words: 41
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A Lie algebra L is perfect when [L,L]=L. Every semisimple Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero is perfect.
Perfectness is a property of a Lie algebra, defined by equality with its commutator algebra; semisimplicity is a sufficient condition in characteristic zero.

Weyl complete reducibility theorem

Words: 189 Articles: 3
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
Every finite-dimensional representation of a complex semisimple Lie algebra is a direct sum of irreducible representations. Equivalently, every invariant subspace has an invariant complement.

Haar averaging produces invariant complements (V=W⊕W⊥)

Words: 60
Weyl complete reducibility theorem OurBigBook.com
For a finite-dimensional continuous complex representation R of a compact group, normalize Haar measure to mass one and average any positive-definite Hermitian inner product:
⟨v,w⟩K​=∫K​⟨R(g)v,R(g)w⟩0​dμ(g).
(1)
The resulting inner product is positive-definite and invariant. If W is an invariant subspace, then W⊥ is invariant as well, since ⟨R(g)v,w⟩K​=⟨v,R(g−1)w⟩K​. Thus V=W⊕W⊥. Restriction to a compact real form, followed by integration of a Lie-algebra representation, proves the Weyl complete reducibility theorem.

Invariant complement from an equivariant projection (V=U⊕kerP)

Words: 44
Weyl complete reducibility theorem OurBigBook.com
If a submodule U of a Lie algebra representation V admits an intertwining map P:V→U with P∣U​=IU​, then P2=P and its kernel is an invariant complement. For a complex semisimple Lie algebra, the Hom representation on maps V→U whose restriction is a scalar identity reduces finding P to splitting of a trivial quotient for a semisimple Lie algebra.

Casimir splitting of a trivial quotient

Words: 64
Weyl complete reducibility theorem OurBigBook.com
In a finite-dimensional short exact sequence 0→N→E→C→0 of representations of a complex semisimple Lie algebra, the generalized zero eigenspace of the Casimir operator maps onto the trivial quotient. All its irreducible composition factors have zero Casimir eigenvalue, so they are trivial. The action is therefore strictly upper triangular and has solvable image; because a semisimple Lie algebra is a perfect Lie algebra, that image is zero. Every lift in this generalized zero eigenspace is invariant, giving a split short exact sequence.

Borel subalgebra

Words: 25
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
For a choice of positive roots, the corresponding Borel subalgebra is b=t⊕n+, the sum of a Cartan subalgebra and all positive root spaces.

Simple Lie algebra

Words: 4k Articles: 91
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A nonabelian Lie algebra is simple when its only ideals are zero and the entire algebra.

Simple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The special linear Lie algebra sln​ consists of the trace-zero n×n matrices with the commutator bracket.

sl2 triple ([h,e]=2e,[h,f]=−2f,[e,f]=h)

Words: 131 Articles: 1
Special linear Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
An sl2 triple consists of elements of a Lie algebra satisfying the displayed brackets. It defines a homomorphism from sl2​ by sending its standard generators to h,e,f. A nonzero homomorphism is injective because sl2​ is a simple Lie algebra. Root vectors and their coroot give such triples in a semisimple Lie algebra, and their representations supply finite weight strings.
Finite sl2 lowest-weight ladder (hXn​=(2n−λ)Xn​,fXn​=n(λ−n+1)Xn−1​)
Words: 78
sl2 triple OurBigBook.com
In a finite-dimensional representation of an sl2 triple, start with a nonzero vector X0​ satisfying fX0​=0 and hX0​=−λX0​, and set Xn​=enX0​. The commutator identities give the displayed weight and lowering formulas by induction. If XN​=0 and XN+1​=0, then fXN+1​=(N+1)(λ−N)XN​ forces λ=N, a nonnegative integer. The nonzero terminal vector is essential: choosing a later index after the ladder has already vanished gives no constraint. Applied to the Adjoint representation of a semisimple Lie algebra, this argument proves integrality of Cartan integers.

Symmetric powers of the defining sln representation (SymmCn=V(mω1​))

Words: 244 Articles: 4
Special linear Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
For n≥2 and m≥0, the representation SymmCn of sln​(C) is irreducible with highest weight mω1​. Its monomial basis supplies weights by adding m defining-representation weights, with repeated weights counted separately.
Contraction splitting of a defining module tensor a dual symmetric square (V⊗Sym2V∗=kerC⊕ι(V∗))
Words: 71
Symmetric powers of the defining sln representation OurBigBook.com
For the defining n-dimensional special linear Lie algebra module, with n≥2, write Ti​(p)=ei​⊗p(y1​,…,yn​). The equivariant contraction is C(Ti​(p))=∂yi​​p. The map ι(f)=∑i​ei​⊗yi​f is also equivariant, since ∑i​ei​⊗yi​ is an invariant identity tensor. Direct differentiation gives Cι=(n+1)I, so the displayed direct sum follows. Its trace-free part is an irreducible representation of highest weight ω1​+2ωn−1​. Its highest-weight vector is e1​⊗yn2​; the Weyl dimension formula gives dimension n(n−1)(n+2)/2, exactly dimkerC.

For a complex semisimple Lie algebra, a Cartan subalgebra is a maximal abelian subalgebra consisting of semisimple elements. It is also called a maximal torus in this setting.

Self-centralizing property of a Cartan subalgebra (CL​(H)=H)

Words: 77
Cartan subalgebra OurBigBook.com
For a Cartan subalgebra H of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra L, H is abelian and CL​(H)=H, so it is maximal among abelian subalgebras. Starting from the nilpotent self-normalizing definition, the generalized-weight decomposition for a nilpotent Lie algebra and the Engel theorem show that the zero generalized weight space of its adjoint action is exactly H. Invariance of the Killing form makes H orthogonal to every nonzero generalized weight space. The Lie theorem gives B([H,H],H)=0, and nondegeneracy then forces [H,H]=0. An element commuting with H normalizes it, hence belongs to H.

Irreducible root system OurBigBook.com
For an irreducible root system spanning V, the span U of a nonzero root's Weyl group orbit is invariant, as is U⊥. A root reflection preserving both subspaces must have its normal entirely in one of them: otherwise its rank-one correction mixes the subspaces. Thus a proper nonzero U would partition all roots into mutually orthogonal subsets, contradicting irreducibility. Consequently some orbit root is nonorthogonal to any given root. Since Weyl reflections preserve lengths, the pairwise integrality restrictions for nonorthogonal roots also bound length ratios of orthogonal roots. All squared-length ratios lie in {1,2,1/2,3,1/3}; there cannot be three distinct lengths, since ratios two and three relative to a shortest root would yield the forbidden ratio 3/2.

Reducedness is a separate axiom; the root-space reducedness lemma establishes it for these Lie-algebra roots.

Root-string theorem
Words: 129
Root string OurBigBook.com
For nonproportional roots γ,δ of a reduced crystallographic root system, Sγ,δ​={δ−pγ,…,δ+qγ} is consecutive, and p−q=⟨δ,γ∨⟩. Realize the crystallographic root system as the roots of a complex semisimple Lie algebra. The sum of the one-dimensional root spaces in this string is a module for the sl2 subalgebra associated with a root. Its weights are ⟨δ,γ∨⟩+2n; they have one fixed parity. Complete reducibility gives a sum of irreducible representations of the sl2 Lie algebra. Two summands of this parity would overlap at weight zero when the parity is even, or at weights ±1 when it is odd, contradicting the one-dimensional root spaces. Thus there is one irreducible string, whose opposite endpoint weights sum to zero. This proves the relation. For distinct simple roots, p=0 and the cardinality is 1−⟨δ,γ∨⟩. Generalized-weight decomposition for a nilpotent Lie algebra (V=⨁λ​Vλ)
Words: 222 Articles: 1
Generalized weight space of a Lie algebra representation OurBigBook.com
Every finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra representation of a nilpotent Lie algebra decomposes into invariant generalized weight spaces. The nilpotence assumption is essential: a general solvable action can have extensions between distinct weights.
Here is a proof. For h,k∈H, nilpotence gives (adh)Nk=0, hence (adρ(h))Nρ(k)=0. By the nilpotent commutator preserves generalized eigenspaces lemma, every generalized eigenspace of ρ(h) is invariant under every ρ(k). Split successively by the acting operators of a basis of H. Each resulting block is invariant under H, and each basis operator has only one eigenvalue on it. The Lie theorem triangularizes the action on each block; its diagonal entries therefore give one and the same linear functional λ on every basis vector of that block. Every ρ(h)−λ(h)I is strictly upper triangular there, proving that the block is Vλ. Distinct blocks have distinct weights, so this is a direct sum. On the zero generalized weight space, every acting operator is a nilpotent endomorphism, so the Engel theorem supplies a nonzero common annihilated vector whenever that space is nonzero.

Let H be a Cartan subalgebra of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra L. In the adjoint generalized-weight decomposition for a nilpotent Lie algebra, its zero summand satisfies L0=H. Nilpotence gives H⊆L0. If L0/H were nonzero, all adjoint operators of H on this quotient would be nilpotent, so the Engel theorem would supply a nonzero coset x+H with [H,x]⊆H. That contradicts self-normalization. The derivation rule ensures that L0 is a subalgebra, so the quotient action is well-defined.

The defining representation of so2n+1​ has weights ε1​,…,εn​,0,−εn​,…,−ε1​. Its crystal basis is a chain on these vertices, with lowering-edge colors 1,…,n−1,n,n,n−1,…,1. The short-root string has length two through zero. With the crystal tensor-product rule, for n≥2 the tensor square has highest vertices 1⊗1, 1⊗2 and 1⊗1ˉ, corresponding to the traceless symmetric square, the exterior square and the trivial Lie algebra representation. Their dimensions are (2n+1)(n+1)−1, n(2n+1) and one.

Root-string property of a crystal

Words: 34
Crystal basis OurBigBook.com
For each simple root αi​, the i-colored edges of a crystal form strings. Along such a string, ei​ raises the weight by αi​ and f​i​ lowers it by αi​.

Kashiwara operator (ei​,f​i​)

Words: 29
Crystal basis OurBigBook.com
On a crystal, f​i​ follows an edge of color i and ei​ follows that edge backwards.
These maps are the raising and lowering operations of a crystal basis.

Tensor product of crystals

Words: 248 Articles: 2
Crystal basis OurBigBook.com
The tensor product crystal uses the i-string data εi​ and φi​ to decide on which tensor factor a Kashiwara operator acts. Its connected components are highest-weight crystals and encode the decomposition of the tensor product representation.
This tensor-product operation combines one crystal basis with another, with factor selection governed by their string parameters.
A2 defining tensor crystals
Words: 121
Tensor product of crystals OurBigBook.com
For the defining representation of the special linear Lie algebra sl3​, the crystal basis is 11​22​3, with weights εi​ restricted to trace-zero diagonal matrices. Its dual is 3ˉ2​2ˉ1​1ˉ, with weights −εi​. Using the crystal tensor-product rule with lowering on the first factor when φi​(a)>εi​(b), the tensor square has highest vertices 1⊗1 and 1⊗2, of highest weights 2ω1​,ω2​, generating components of six and three vertices. The defining tensor dual has highest vertices 1⊗3ˉ and 1⊗1ˉ, generating components of eight and one vertices and weights ω1​+ω2​,0. These encode the symmetric square plus exterior square, and the trace-free endomorphisms plus scalar identity, respectively. A crystal vertex labelled by a tensor pair need not represent that same undeformed ordinary simple tensor; the actual invariant vector is ∑i​ei​⊗ei∗​.
Crystal tensor-product rule
Words: 77
Tensor product of crystals OurBigBook.com
Write εi​(b) and φi​(b) for the numbers of raising and lowering steps of color i available from a vertex of a crystal basis. One convention for the tensor product of crystals is
f​i​(a⊗b)={f​i​(a)⊗b,a⊗f​i​(b),​φi​(a)>εi​(b),φi​(a)≤εi​(b).​
(55)
The raising operator uses the first factor for φi​(a)≥εi​(b) and the second otherwise. The different strictness makes raising and lowering inverse along every edge. An edge is absent if the chosen Kashiwara operator vanishes. Stating the convention is essential when identifying the highest-weight vectors as ordered tensor vertices.

Casimir element

Words: 367 Articles: 6
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The quadratic Casimir element is a central element of U(g). On a highest-weight module of highest weight λ, one standard normalization makes it act by ∣λ+ρ∣2−∣ρ∣2.

Quadratic Casimir operator (∑a​ta​ta​=C2​(R)I)

Words: 276 Articles: 3
Casimir element OurBigBook.com
For a Lie algebra representation with generators referred to an orthonormal invariant form, the sum ∑a​ta​ta​ commutes with every generator. Indeed, the commutator is proportional to a contraction of antisymmetric structure constants of a Lie algebra with the symmetric product ta​tb​+tb​ta​. The Schur lemma makes it scalar in an irreducible complex representation; that scalar is its quadratic Casimir eigenvalue. With trace normalization tr(ta​tb​)=C(R)δab​, taking the trace gives C(R)dimg=C2​(R)dimR.

SU(3) Casimir in Chevalley generators (C=3C2​)

Words: 55
Quadratic Casimir operator OurBigBook.com
For e3​=[e1​,e2​], f3​=−[f1​,f2​], the operator C=h12​+h22​+h1​h2​+3(h1​+h2​)+3∑i=13​fi​ei​ commutes with all generators. In its commutator with e1​, the Cartan polynomial contributes 3h1​e1​, while the last sum contributes −3h1​e1​; the two mixed terms involving f2​e3​ cancel. On highest weight (p,q) its eigenvalue is p2+q2+pq+3p+3q. This normalization is three times the conventional SU(3) quadratic Casimir eigenvalue.

SU(3) quadratic Casimir eigenvalue (C2​(a,b)=(a2+ab+b2+3a+3b)/3)

Words: 85
Quadratic Casimir operator OurBigBook.com
For generators normalized by tr3​(ta​tb​)=δab​/2, the quadratic Casimir operator on the irreducible SU(3) representation of Dynkin labels (a,b) has the displayed scalar value. In SU(3) highest-weight coordinates (p,q) it is p2+q2+p+3​q.
To derive this, write the operator as H12​+H22​+∑i=13​(E+i​E−i​+E−i​E+i​). On a highest-weight vector, the raising operators vanish, and the three root commutators sum to H1​+3​H2​. Centrality and the Schur lemma extend this value to the representation. The singlet, fundamental, adjoint and decuplet values are 0,4/3,3,6, respectively. Tensor labels and multiplet dimensions are summarized in the Particle Data Group's SU(n) multiplet guide.

Tensor-product Casimir trace identity (∑i​d(Ri​)C2​(Ri​)=d(R1​)d(R2​)[C2​(R1​)+C2​(R2​)])

Words: 78
Quadratic Casimir operator OurBigBook.com
For traceless generators, the tensor product of Lie algebra representations has generators ta​⊗I+I⊗sa​. The trace of their summed squares is the sum of the two factor Casimir traces; the cross term vanishes because trta​=trsa​=0. Decomposition into irreducible representations, with multiplicities counted, gives the displayed identity. Without tracelessness an extra term 2∑a​trta​trsa​ is present. A one-dimensional abelian representation of charge one tensored with itself has Casimir four, not the sum two; semisimple Lie algebras avoid this problem because every generator is a sum of commutators.

Casimir eigenvalue (cλ​=(λ,λ+2ρ))

Words: 36
Casimir element OurBigBook.com
The Casimir operator formed from the Killing form acts on an Irreducible Lie algebra representation with highest weight λ by the scalar (λ,λ+2ρ), where ρ is the half-sum of positive roots. It is zero on the trivial Lie algebra representation and nonzero on every nontrivial finite-dimensional irreducible complex representation of a semisimple Lie algebra.

Casimir eigenvalue for sl2 (21​m(m+2))

Words: 25
Casimir element OurBigBook.com
For sl2​ with [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=−2f, and [e,f]=h, the Casimir
Ω=ef+fe+21​h2
(56)
acts on the irreducible highest-weight module V(m) by the scalar 21​m(m+2).

Principal sl2 subalgebra (sl2pr​)

Words: 154 Articles: 2
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A principal sl2 subalgebra of a semisimple Lie algebra has semisimple generator hpr​=2ρ∨. Restriction to it packages a representation's weights into ordinary sl2​ weight strings.
The infinitesimal embedding is a subalgebra of the semisimple Lie algebra; integrating it to a Lie-group homomorphism is a separate group-level construction.

Construction of a principal sl2 triple (e=∑i​ei​,h=2ρ∨,f=∑i​ci​fi​)

Words: 71
Principal sl2 subalgebra OurBigBook.com
Choose simple root vectors with [ei​,fi​]=hi​=αi∨​, and let ρ∨ be the half-sum of positive coroots. It satisfies αi​(ρ∨)=1. Expand h=2ρ∨=∑i​ci​hi​. For i=j, [ei​,fj​]=0, since the difference of distinct simple roots is not a root of a root system. Thus [e,f]=h, while [h,e]=2e and [h,f]=−2f. These identities construct an embedded sl2 Lie algebra in any nonzero complex semisimple Lie algebra. Its raising vector is the principal nilpotent element with a nonzero component in each simple-root space.

Principal nilpotent element

Words: 39
Principal sl2 subalgebra OurBigBook.com
A principal nilpotent element of a semisimple Lie algebra is a nilpotent element whose centralizer has dimension equal to the rank. For nonzero simple-root vectors ei​, the sum e=∑i​ei​ is principal nilpotent and forms the raising element of a Principal sl2 subalgebra.

Weight (representation theory)

Words: 48
Semisimple Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A weight of a representation is a simultaneous eigenvalue functional for a commuting Cartan subalgebra. In general algebra representations it can be expressed as a one-dimensional character of the acting commutative algebra. A weight vector is an eigenvector carrying that functional; a weight space is the corresponding eigenspace, and weight multiplicity is its dimension.
